findings.detail: The question repeats earlier question M2-S11-T1 in the same research-system setting. Both are about a changed function signature behind a wrapper module, and the two correct answers are the same two steps restated as gaps: list every export of the wrapper, and Grep for each name across the whole codebase. The same reasoning leads to the answer. Several wrong options also repeat. Option A is the same 'Read every file upfront' distractor. Option D is the same idea as the earlier 'search only for the original function name' distractor. Option E reuses the Glob-misuse distractor. The rule allows at most one repeated wrong option.

blind_answer.reason: Tracing usage through a wrapper module means listing every name it exports and then searching for each of those names across the whole codebase (2.5-S5). The trace recorded only format_reference, so build_bibliography was missed (C). It also limited Grep to the synthesis subagent's directory, so the report subagent's call was never searched (B). A describes the anti-pattern of reading every file upfront. D is wrong because calls through the wrapper are real usage. E reverses the tools: Grep searches file contents and Glob matches file paths.
